episodes.title: Quodlibet 31: Are We Obligated to Assent to Non-Infallible Church Teaching?
episodes.short: Quodlibet 31: Are We Obligated to Assent to Non-Infallible Church Teaching?
episodes.description: Do We Have to Assent to Non-Infallible Church Teaching? What are the different ways in which the Church teaches? Are they all infallible? Why does matter have to be the principle of individuation? What do the mystical theologians mean by the phrase "quasi-experimental" contemplation? How should we judge the morality of new and emerging medical technologies like therapeutic brain implants and augmented perception? Do the guys like Halloween? Join us for these questions and more!

episodes.title: Blessed Fulton Sheen
episodes.short: Blessed Fulton Sheen
episodes.description: Dr. Matthew Kuhner and Dr. Edmund Lazzari join Dr. Matthew Vander Vennet to discuss Blessed Fulton Sheen's philosophy, theology, life, and contributions to the Catholic Church in the United States and beyond.

episodes.title: Quodlibet 30: Do You Need to Confess Even After an Act of Perfect Contrition?
episodes.short: Quodlibet 30: Do You Need to Confess Even After an Act of Perfect Contrition?
episodes.description: Do You Need to Confess Even After an Act of Perfect Contrition? How does Catholic theology understand savantism? Is this a good or a privation of a good? How do different Catholics views on grace and free will shape prayer and devotion? Join us for these questions and more.

episodes.title: Saint Francis and the Franciscan School
episodes.short: Saint Francis and the Franciscan School
episodes.description: Fr Charles A M Robinson, FI and Dr. Joey Belleza join Fr. Dylan Schrader to discuss St. Francis of Assisi and the Franciscan theological tradition in honor of the 800th anniversary of St. Francis's death.

episodes.title: Quodlibet 29: Was Mary Able to Sin?
episodes.short: Quodlibet 29: Was Mary Able to Sin?
episodes.description: We know that Mary never sinned, but was she able to do so? What's the use of studying theology? Can't the unlearned know just as much about God? How ought a Catholic to explain the Church's teaching on IVF? Join us for these questions and more!

episodes.title: Quodlibet 28: Should AI Be Used for Sacred Art?
episodes.short: Quodlibet 28: Should AI Be Used for Sacred Art?
episodes.description: We're back after an unintended summer hiatus! Should AI be used for sacred art? If the Incarnation begins at the Annunciation, why is Christmas the more important liturgical day? If receiving the Eucharist removes venial sins, is it wrong to go to confession immediately after receiving (if one is not aware of having sinned mortally)? Is it acceptable for a Catholic to work for a military defense contractor? Join us for these questions and more!

episodes.title: Private Revelations?
episodes.short: Private Revelations?
episodes.description: Dr. Matthew Minerd and Fr. Ambrose Dobrozsi join Fr. Dylan Schrader to discuss private revelations, including their relationship to public revelation, what level of assent they require, and some speculative questions.

episodes.title: All About Bishops with Bishop Fredrik Hansen
episodes.short: All About Bishops with Bishop Fredrik Hansen
episodes.description: The Most Rev. Fredrik Hansen, Bishop of Oslo and a canon lawyer, joins Fr. Dylan Schrader to discuss the role of bishops in the Catholic Church. What is the college of bishops? How are bishops chosen? How do bishops relate to the pope? and more in this special episode of Sed Contra!

episodes.title: Sacraments as Signs
episodes.short: Sacraments as Signs
episodes.description: Fr. Dylan Schrader and Dr. Joey Belleza discuss sacraments as signs, including how they work, how the Church analyzes the parts of the sacramental sign, pastoral issues, and the question of "Ecclesia supplet."

episodes.title: Quodlibet 27: Could There Be Divinely Inspired Texts That Didnt Make It Into the Bible?
episodes.short: Quodlibet 27: Could There Be Divinely Inspired Texts That Didnt Make It Into the Bible?
episodes.description: Could there be divinely-inspired texts that didn't make it into the canon of Sacred Scripture? Could the Church amend the sacraments in order to evangelize extra-terrestrials? Does Down Syndrome remain in heaven? Why would God create a soul that He foreknows will end up in hell? Join us for these questions and more!

episodes.title: The Hymns of Corpus Christi
episodes.short: The Hymns of Corpus Christi
episodes.description: Dr. Joey Belleza and Fr. Ambrose Dobrozsi dig into the poetry of St. Thomas Aquinas' Eucharistic hymns for the feast of Corpus Christi.

episodes.title: Quodlibet 26: Do All Dogs Go to Heaven?
episodes.short: Quodlibet 26: Do All Dogs Go to Heaven?
episodes.description: Is it possible for animals to go to heaven? Is chewing gum for pleasure a sin? Do habitual grave sins count as mortal sin? Join us for these questions and more!

episodes.title: Aquinas, the Bible, and the Fathers
episodes.short: Aquinas, the Bible, and the Fathers
episodes.description: Fr. Ambrose Dobrozsi, Dr. Kevin Clarke, and Dr. Jane Peters talk about St. Thomas Aquinas' Catena Aurea commentary on the Gospels

episodes.title: Quodlibet 25: Does God Know the Taste of Orange Chicken?
episodes.short: Quodlibet 25: Does God Know the Taste of Orange Chicken?
episodes.description: Does God know what Panda Express Orange Chicken tastes like? Does changing a baby's diaper during consecration mean that you have not fulfilled your Sunday obligation? Why have recent popes seemed to condemn war so often? Does Catholicism require pascifism? Join us for these questions and more!

episodes.title: Quodlibet 24: Is Chewing Gum Contrary to Nature?
episodes.short: Quodlibet 24: Is Chewing Gum Contrary to Nature?
episodes.description: Is chewing gum contrary to the faculty of digestion? Are violent sports like football, boxing, or MMA sinful? What is "personalism," and is it consonant with Catholic teaching? Join us for these questions and more!

episodes.title: Divine Mercy and Indulgences
episodes.short: Divine Mercy and Indulgences
episodes.description: Is there a special promise on Divine Mercy Sunday that you can get remission of the temporal punishment due to sin without the typical requirements for an indulgence? Fr. Ambrose Dobrozsi and Fr. Dylan Schrader dig into this question and discuss the nature of indulgences, sin, punishment, and God's abundant mercy.

episodes.title: Can one be saved apart from or outside the Church?
episodes.short: Can one be saved apart from or outside the Church?
episodes.description: Aaron Debusschere and Fr. Ambrose Dobrozsi take up the question of salvation. Can someone outside the Church be saved? Is salvation something individual or communal?

episodes.title: Quodlibet 23: Are There Any Good Arguments for Sedevacantism?
episodes.short: Quodlibet 23: Are There Any Good Arguments for Sedevacantism?
episodes.description: Are there any good arguments for sedevacantism? Why is fasting so important, and how does it relate to the gift of final perseverance? How can you encourage your husband to take a more active interest in the Faith? How do we overcome sloth? Join us for these questions and more!

episodes.title: Quodlibet 22: Why Isn't the Washing of Feet a Sacrament?
episodes.short: Quodlibet 22: Why Isn't the Washing of Feet a Sacrament?
episodes.description: Why isn't the ritual of pedelavium or foot washing considered a sacrament? Could the Church discover a new sacrament? What is the best method for interpreting Scripture today? Does the historical-critical method have a place? Join us for these questions and more!

episodes.title: Quodlibet 21: Are Magnanimity and Humility Opposed?
episodes.short: Quodlibet 21: Are Magnanimity and Humility Opposed?
episodes.description: Are magnanimity and humility opposed? Can you be both? How would it be just for a soul that dies only with original sin to be damned? Does St. Thomas make a distinction between intellect and mind? Join us for these questions and more!

episodes.title: Does Changing Liturgy Change the Faith?
episodes.short: Does Changing Liturgy Change the Faith?
episodes.description: Fr. Ambrose Dobrozsi, Dr. Matthew Minerd, and Christopher Owens talk about the connection of liturgy to theology based on the traditional dictum, lex orandi lex credendi.

episodes.title: Quodlibet 20: Should the Church Promote Only One Theological School?
episodes.short: Quodlibet 20: Should the Church Promote Only One Theological School?
episodes.description: Why doesn't the Church promote only one theological school as the most accurate? How do we reconcile what we know now about animal intelligence with a Thomistic understanding of the soul? What is your favorite work of non-fiction? Join us for these questions and more!

episodes.title: Quodlibet 19: Are Arguments from Authority the Strongest?
episodes.short: Quodlibet 19: Are Arguments from Authority the Strongest?
episodes.description: Are arguments from authority the strongest in theology? Is it possible that humans exist without an eternal soul? Join us for these questions and more!

episodes.title: Quodlibet 18: Are there Male and Female Souls?
episodes.short: Quodlibet 18: Are there Male and Female Souls?
episodes.description: Are there male and female souls? What is distributism, and does it align with Catholic social teaching? A la Monty Python, which country's historical philosophers would field the best soccer team? All that and more on this episode of The Quodlibets!

episodes.title: Is Ratzinger Right? Theology and History IV
episodes.short: Is Ratzinger Right? Theology and History IV
episodes.description: The last in our series on theology and history, this episode dives in to the theology of Joseph Ratzinger (Pope Benedict XVI) and his account of the theology of history in St. Bonaventure.

episodes.title: Quodlibets 17 : How did St. Michael and Lucifer Duke it Out?
episodes.short: Quodlibets 17 : How did St. Michael and Lucifer Duke it Out?
episodes.description: How exactly did St. Michael and Lucifer duke it out? Does God have emotions? Join us for these questions and more!

episodes.title: The Dies Irae and Christian Hope
episodes.short: The Dies Irae and Christian Hope
episodes.description: Fr. Ambrose Dobrozsi and Dr. Joey Belleza discuss the Dies Irae and the unity between fear of judgement and Christian hope

episodes.title: Thinking About the Virtue of Faith with St Thomas Part II
episodes.short: Thinking About the Virtue of Faith with St Thomas Part II
episodes.description: Dr. Brandon Wanless, Molly Egilsrud, and Fr. John Wilson discuss the virtue of Faith from the perspective of St. Thomas Aquinas. Part 2 of 2.

episodes.title: Theology and History III
episodes.short: Theology and History III
episodes.description: The third in our series on theology and history, this episode discusses what theology has to say about history. Fr. Ambrose, Dr. Timothy Kearns, and Dr. Kevin Clarke join up to talk about the history of history and what theology can contribute.

episodes.title: Thinking About the Virtue of Faith with St Thomas Part I
episodes.short: Thinking About the Virtue of Faith with St Thomas Part I
episodes.description: Dr. Brandon Wanless, Molly Egilsrud, and Fr. John Wilson discuss the virtue of Faith from the perspective of St. Thomas Aquinas. Part 1 of 2.

episodes.title: Theology and History II
episodes.short: Theology and History II
episodes.description: Fr. Ambrose Dobrozsi, John O'Neill, and Elliot Polsky come together for the second episode in our series on theology and history. This second episode discusses the extent to which historical particulars can enter into the object of sacred theology, properly speaking.

episodes.title: The Theology of Fr. Peter Damian Fehlner
episodes.short: The Theology of Fr. Peter Damian Fehlner
episodes.description: This episode discusses the contributions of the little-known Fr. Peter Damian Fehlner, possibly the greatest Franciscan theologian of the post-conciliar times.

episodes.title: Theology and History I
episodes.short: Theology and History I
episodes.description: The first in a multi-part series on theology and history. In this first part, we examine how historical study can support the work of theology.

episodes.title: Corpus Christi
episodes.short: Corpus Christi
episodes.description: Today on Sed Contra, the Sacra Doctrina Project's Joey Belleza is joined by Alexander Masir, for a discussion of the solemnity of Corpus Christi.

episodes.title: What the Meaning of the Word 'Is' Is
episodes.short: What the Meaning of the Word 'Is' Is
episodes.description: Today on Sed Contra, the Sacra Doctrina Project's Elliot Polsky and Urban Hannon discuss three medieval theories of the meaning of the word "is," and what difference this makes to contemporary discussions of "esse."

episodes.title: Why Should I Care About St. Bonaventure
episodes.short: Why Should I Care About St. Bonaventure
episodes.description: Today on Sed Contra, the Sacra Doctrina Project's Joey Belleza is joined by Fr. Clinton Sensat, of the Diocese of Lafayette, for a discussion on St. Bonaventure of Bagnoregio.

episodes.title: The Modern Turn to the Subject
episodes.short: The Modern Turn to the Subject
episodes.description: Today on Sed Contra, SDP members Fr. Ambrose Dobrozsi, Elliot Polsky, and Pater Edmund Waldstein discuss the modern turn to the subject, as well as its various philosophical, cultural, and religious implications.

episodes.title: Can Gender Change?
episodes.short: Can Gender Change?
episodes.description: Today on Sed Contra, SDP members Fr. Ambrose Dobrozsi, Daniel Drain, and Kara Johnson discuss gender and sex. They consider these in the light of the Catholic theological tradition, with special attention to St. Thomas Aquinas and Pope Francis.

episodes.title: God's Happiness
episodes.short: God's Happiness
episodes.description: In this Sed Contra podcast episode, the discussion centers on the Beatitude of God. The episode is hosted by Pater Edmund Waldstein, O.Cist., who is a monk of the Cistercian Abbey of Stift Heiligenkreuz in Austria and an ordinary member of the Sacra Doctrina Project, with fellow ordinary SDP member Urban Hannon who is a seminarian of the FSSP and a doctoral student at the University of Fribourg, and special guest Fr. Sebastian Walshe, O.Praem., is a Norbertine Canon of the Abbey of St. Michaelin the Diocese of Orange, California. For those interested, Fr. Sebastian has published an academic ar

episodes.title: Disputed Question on Frozen Embryo Adoption
episodes.short: Disputed Question on Frozen Embryo Adoption
episodes.description: The return of the disputed question Sed Contra episode. Join host James W. Stroud along with SDP board members Daniel Lendman and Matthew Dugandzic as they take opposing sides in response to this disputed question on the Catholic position regarding frozen embryo adoption.

episodes.title: Aliens and Soteriology
episodes.short: Aliens and Soteriology
episodes.description: In this episode of Sed Contra, SDP members Dr. John Brungardt, Dr. Kevin Clarke, and Dr. Taylor Patrick O'Neill are joined by guest Rev. Dr. Andrew Davison to discuss aliens and soteriology. Rev. Dr. Davison is the Starbridge Professor of Theology and Natural Sciences in the Faculty of Divinity at the University of Cambridge, and Fellow in Theology and Dean of Chapel at Corpus Christi and soon to be Canon and Regius Professor of Divinity at Christ Church Oxford (appointed June 2024 by His Majesty King Charles III). He recently authored Astrobiology and Christian Doctrine: Exploring the Implica

episodes.title: The Most Holy Eucharist and Transubstantiation
episodes.short: The Most Holy Eucharist and Transubstantiation
episodes.description: In this extended episode of Sed Contra, Urban Hannon and Joey Belleza discuss the Most Holy Eucharist and in particular transubstantiation with careful attention to St. Thomas Aquinas' articulation of this doctrine in the Summa theologiae III, q. 75.

episodes.title: Why Should I Care About Balthasar
episodes.short: Why Should I Care About Balthasar
episodes.description: In this Sed Contra podcast episode, Why Should I Care About Balthasar, join Sacra Doctrina Project members Dr. Kevin Clarke and Mr. Daniel Drain and special guest Dr. Mark Spencer as they discuss the relevance and importance of the works of Hans Urs von Balthasar.

episodes.title: The Quest for the Historical St. Thomas Aquinas
episodes.short: The Quest for the Historical St. Thomas Aquinas
episodes.description: In this newest Sed Contra episode join Fr. Cajetan Cuddy, O.P., Dr. Matthew Minerd, and Dr. James W. Stroud as they discuss the Quest for the Historical St. Thomas Aquinas, its roots and its impact on Catholic philosophy and theology.

episodes.title: The Life and Work of Bl. Columba Marmion, OSB
episodes.short: The Life and Work of Bl. Columba Marmion, OSB
episodes.description: Dr. Matthew Minerd, Pater Edmund Waldstein, O.Cist., and Dr. Danny Garland discuss the life and work of Blessed Columba Marmion, O.S.B.

episodes.title: Maximus the Confessor and Why Catholics Should Care about Him
episodes.short: Maximus the Confessor and Why Catholics Should Care about Him
episodes.description: Dr. Kevin Clarke, Dr. Joseph Terry, and Dr. John Solheid discuss Maximus the Confessor and why Catholics should be familiar with his life and work.

episodes.title: NFP and the Supposed Contraceptive Mentality
episodes.short: NFP and the Supposed Contraceptive Mentality
episodes.description: Dr. Matthew Dugandzic, Dr. Taylor Patrick O'Neill, P. Edmund Waldstein, O.Cist., and Dr. James Stroud discuss NFP, contraception, and the contraceptive mentality.

episodes.title: Differences in Eucharistic Piety Among Roman and Byzantine Catholics
episodes.short: Differences in Eucharistic Piety Among Roman and Byzantine Catholics
episodes.description: Dr. Matthew Dugandzic, Dr. Danny Garland, and Dr. Ryan Brady discuss the differences in Eucharistic piety among Roman and Byzantine Catholics. Includes an epilogue by Dr. Kevin Clarke.

episodes.title: Artificial Intelligence
episodes.short: Artificial Intelligence
episodes.description: Dr. Kevin Clarke and Dr. John Solheid discuss artificial intelligence with Fr. Dylan Schrader

episodes.title: Laudato si'
episodes.short: Laudato si'
episodes.description: Dr. James Stroud, Dr. John Macias, Dr. Taylor Patrick O'Neill, and Fr. Dylan Schrader discuss Pope Francis's 2015 Encyclical Laudato si', on the care of our common home.

episodes.title: Veritatis Splendor at 30
episodes.short: Veritatis Splendor at 30
episodes.description: Dr. James Stroud and P. Edmund Waldstein, O.Cist., discuss the watershed encyclical of St. John Paul II on moral theology, Veritatis splendor (The Splendor of Truth) as the Church approaches the thirtieth anniversary of its promulgation.

episodes.title: Further Musings on Universalism
episodes.short: Further Musings on Universalism
episodes.description: Dr. John Solheid and Dr. Kevin Clarke muse on Origen, apocatastasis, and the issues surrounding the issue with Fr. Dylan Schrader.

episodes.title: The Ascension
episodes.short: The Ascension
episodes.description: Fr. Dylan Schrader and Dr. Kevin Clarke discuss the dogma of Christ's Ascension into heaven, its significance, its connection with other mysteries, and where Jesus is now.

episodes.title: Intrinsic Evils
episodes.short: Intrinsic Evils
episodes.description: Dr. Matthew Dugandzic and Dr. Ryan Brady discuss intrinsic evils.

episodes.title: Gaven Kerr on the Fifth Way
episodes.short: Gaven Kerr on the Fifth Way
episodes.description: Dr. Gaven Kerr discusses St. Thomas Aquinas's Fifth Way (from the governance of things) to demonstrate the existence of God.

episodes.title: Tribute to Joseph Ratzinger / Benedict XVI
episodes.short: Tribute to Joseph Ratzinger / Benedict XVI
episodes.description: Sacra Doctrina Project members discuss Joseph Ratzinger / Benedict XVI and pay tribute to him at his passing from this life. May he rest in peace.

episodes.title: 2022 Movie Draft
episodes.short: 2022 Movie Draft
episodes.description: Sacra Doctrina Project members propose and discuss their line-ups of movies in these categories: Christmas; Family Drama; Psychological Thriller; Foreign Language; Catholic; and 2022 Movie.

episodes.title: Divine Impassibility
episodes.short: Divine Impassibility
episodes.description: Doctors Matthew Dugandzic and Kevin Clarke discuss divine impassibility and related divine attributes (such as immutability) with Father Dylan Schrader.

episodes.title: Why Can't Christ Be a Human Person?
episodes.short: Why Can't Christ Be a Human Person?
episodes.description: Doctors Daniel Garland and Kevin Clarke discuss with Fr. Dylan Schrader why Christ isn't and can't be a human person.

episodes.title: Chalcedonian Christology and the Concept of Pure Nature
episodes.short: Chalcedonian Christology and the Concept of Pure Nature
episodes.description: In this special episode, Fr. Thomas Joseph White, OP, speaks about Chalcedonian Christology and the concept of pure nature. This was a keynote address given at the 2022 Sacra Doctrina Project annual conference.

episodes.title: Grace and the City: Infused Moral Virtues and Common Goods
episodes.short: Grace and the City: Infused Moral Virtues and Common Goods
episodes.description: In this special episode Dr. Patrick Gardner speaks about the infused moral virtues and the common good. This was a plenary address given at the 2022 Sacra Doctrina Project annual conference.

episodes.title: Truth, Freedom, and the Catholic University
episodes.short: Truth, Freedom, and the Catholic University
episodes.description: Dr. John G. Brungardt and Dr. Kevin Clarke discuss truth and academic freedom in the context of the contemporary Catholic university. Listen as they explore the historic Land O'Lakes document, its impact on how the Catholic university understands itself, and the response it has elicited over the past 55 years.

episodes.title: Aquinas and the Bible
episodes.short: Aquinas and the Bible
episodes.description: Fr. Dylan Schrader and Dr. Daniel Garland discuss Thomas Aquinas and the Bible along with biblical theology and the historical critical method today.

episodes.title: Theological Manuals Revisited
episodes.short: Theological Manuals Revisited
episodes.description: Drs. Ryan Brady and Matthew Dugandzic are joined by the prolific author and translator, Dr. Matthew Minerd, to continue the discussion about theological manuals, including his recent translation of Reginald Garrigou-Lagrange's De Revelatione.

episodes.title: Theological Manuals?
episodes.short: Theological Manuals?
episodes.description: Dr. Matthew Dugandzic and Dr. Ryan Brady discuss theological manuals and the manualist tradition. Why are they so often criticized, and are these criticisms fair? Were the manuals destructive of real theology, or is it time to revive them?

episodes.title: Private Revelation
episodes.short: Private Revelation
episodes.description: Fr. Dylan Schrader and Dr. Kevin Clarke discuss private revelation.

episodes.title: Irenaeus of Lyons: The Church’s Newest Oldest Doctor
episodes.short: Irenaeus of Lyons: The Church’s Newest Oldest Doctor
episodes.description: This month, Pope Francis announced that Irenaeus of Lyons (130-202) would be declared a doctor of the Church. Daniel Lendman, Ryan Brady, and Kevin Clarke discuss the theology of St. Irenaeus as well as the fittingness of this declaration.

episodes.title: Is the Perverted Faculty Argument Sound?
episodes.short: Is the Perverted Faculty Argument Sound?
episodes.description: Fr. Dylan Schrader moderates a discussion among Matthew Dugandzic, William Diem, and Ryan Brady on the question of whether the perverted faculty argument can be used to produce sound moral judgments.

episodes.title: Is Mary Co-Redemptrix? Is She Mediatrix of All Graces?
episodes.short: Is Mary Co-Redemptrix? Is She Mediatrix of All Graces?
episodes.description: On this episode, Drs. Kevin Clarke, William Diem, Daniel Lendman, and Taylor Patrick O'Neill discuss the Marian titles of "Co-Redemptrix" and "Mediatrix of all Graces." Can the titles be applied to Mary? What precisely do the titles designate? The participants debate the precise meaning of the titles and consider whether the Church should formally declare them.

episodes.title: A Discourse on Vocations
episodes.short: A Discourse on Vocations
episodes.description: When Daniel Lendman, Christopher Owens, and Fr. Dylan Schrader discuss Church vocations from a theological perspective, disagreements and distinctions abound.

episodes.title: Would God Have Become Incarnate Had Man Not Sinned?
episodes.short: Would God Have Become Incarnate Had Man Not Sinned?
episodes.description: In this episode we discuss the motive of the Incarnation. Would God have become incarnate had man not fallen into sin? Drs. Kevin Clarke, Daniel Lendman, Taylor Patrick O'Neill, and Fr. Dylan Schrader discuss.

episodes.title: The Morality of Lying
episodes.short: The Morality of Lying
episodes.description: On this episode, Dr. Matthew Dugandzic discusses the morality of lying with Frs. Dylan Schrader and Jon Tveit.

episodes.title: Do We Always Choose What Seems Best?
episodes.short: Do We Always Choose What Seems Best?
episodes.description: In this episode, Drs. William Diem, Matthew Dugandzic, Taylor Patrick O'Neill, and Fr. Dylan Schrader discuss the question of whether we always choose what we perceive to be the higher good. Does the will always follow the intellect? Is this a form of intellectual determinism?

episodes.title: On Usury
episodes.short: On Usury
episodes.description: On this episode, Dr. William Diem, Dr. Matthew Dugandzic, and Fr. Dylan Schrader discuss usury and the morality of loaning at interest.

episodes.title: The Theology of the Immaculate Conception
episodes.short: The Theology of the Immaculate Conception
episodes.description: On this episode, Fr. Dylan Schrader, Matthew Dugandzic, and Taylor Patrick O'Neill discuss the Immaculate Conception.

episodes.title: The Passions of the Christ
episodes.short: The Passions of the Christ
episodes.description: We're back! On this episode, Fr. Dylan Schrader and Dr. Matthew Dugandžić discuss what the passions are according to Aquinas and how the passions of Christ are similar and different to those we experience.

episodes.title: Molinism vs. Báñezianism: A Debate
episodes.short: Molinism vs. Báñezianism: A Debate
episodes.description: In this episode, Fr. Dylan Schrader moderates a debate between Dr. William Diem and Dr. Taylor Patrick O'Neill who argue on behalf of Molinism and Báñezianism, respectively. Does God move the will directly? How does the scientia media relate to divine omnipotence? Are there any overlaps between the thought of Molina and Báñez? Join us for consideration of those questions and more. Also, you may know leave us a voicemail with questions or comments that we will feature in our next episode. Call 319-382-0886 to leave us a message.

episodes.title: On the Extraordinary Minister of Sacraments and the Sacrament of Penance
episodes.short: On the Extraordinary Minister of Sacraments and the Sacrament of Penance
episodes.description: On this episode, we consider whether the priest is properly understood as the extraordinary minister of the sacrament of penance. What is the nature of an extraordinary minister of a sacrament in the first place? We also consider these questions in light of ecclesiological questions, as well as the place of the sacrament of penance in the life of the Church.

episodes.title: Are the Bride and Groom Really the Ministers of the Sacrament of Matrimony?
episodes.short: Are the Bride and Groom Really the Ministers of the Sacrament of Matrimony?
episodes.description: On this episode of Sed Contra, Brandon Wanless, Daniel Lendman, and Taylor Patrick O'Neill are joined by Fr. Dylan Schrader. They discuss some of the uniqueness of the sacrament of marriage and question whether there are truly any ministers for this sacrament. They also discuss the signification of marriage and the relation between natural and sacramental marriage.

episodes.title: Is the Crucifixion Necessary? (And Will the Entire Created Order be Saved?)
episodes.short: Is the Crucifixion Necessary? (And Will the Entire Created Order be Saved?)
episodes.description: In this third episode of Sed Contra, we discuss Elizabeth Johnson's interview with US Catholic wherein she claims that no one had to die for our sins. Is that correct? Is the entire created order saved? Does Christ become incarnate as man alone or in a more general sense as body or flesh? Can animals be resurrected as man is? We explore these and other issues in this episode.

episodes.title: Contra Universalism (and Is This the Best of All Possible Worlds?)
episodes.short: Contra Universalism (and Is This the Best of All Possible Worlds?)
episodes.description: On this month's episode, five of the six founding members of The Sacra Doctrina Project meet to discuss the doctrine of universalism. What is it? Does it have a basis in the Catholic theological tradition? Recent versions of universalism are contrasted with the seminal work Dare We Hope? by Hans Urs von Balthasar. Finally, the hosts debate whether this is really the best of all possible worlds.

episodes.title: Compendia 01: How Can God Move the Will Infallibly and Yet Contingently?
episodes.short: Compendia 01: How Can God Move the Will Infallibly and Yet Contingently?
episodes.description: Join us for our first episode of Compendia, a new series of mini-episodes of the Sed Contra podcast. In this episode, Dr. Taylor Patrick O'Neill will consider how St. Thomas Aquinas can maintain that God infallibly moves the human will (such as in the case of actual grace) but without imposing any necessity on the human will (and thus without falling into the errors of Calvinism or Jansenism).

episodes.title: What is Sacra Doctrina?
episodes.short: What is Sacra Doctrina?
episodes.description: The inaugural episode of Sed Contra: A Podcast of Catholic Theology. In this episode, we explore the notion of "sacra doctrina." Is it the same thing as theology? Is it merely practical or pastoral? All of that and more.
